objective:
Task SS4.4: Rewrite the 'Continue or stop' subsection of `.claude/commands/continue-development.md` (under its 'Delegate -> Verify -> Track -> Continue-or-stop loop' heading, the last subsection in that loop) to replace its subjective 'substantial batch' stopping language with the configured run budgets from `.sdlc/project.yaml`'s `budgets` block, plus explicit unconditional-stop conditions. Condensed design context you need (do not read design-spec.md/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md yourself -- this is already distilled for you):

1. WHERE THE BUDGETS LIVE: `.sdlc/project.yaml` (in your read_paths -- read the actual file, don't guess the values) has a `budgets` block with: `max_tasks_per_run` (an integer cap on how many tasks this orchestrator run completes before stopping), `max_concurrent_implementers` (already enforced elsewhere in the Delegate section -- just reference it here, don't re-explain the mechanism), `max_attempts_per_task` (a cap on how many times a single task gets retried before it escalates to the orchestrator's own judgment instead of continuing to retry automatically), `max_verifier_retries` (same idea, for verifier-agent retries specifically), and `token_or_time_budget` (a nested `tokens`/`minutes` pair, explicitly a SOFT budget -- logged and flagged when it looks like it's being exceeded, never a hard kill, since Claude Code has no clean mid-run cutoff primitive to enforce it with). These values are `.sdlc/project.yaml`'s current numbers as of this writing; the rewritten text must say to READ them from the file at run time, not hardcode the specific numbers you see today -- a future edit to `project.yaml` should change orchestrator behavior without needing a matching edit to this command file.

2. THIS APPLIES REGARDLESS OF TRACKING CONVENTION: `.sdlc/project.yaml` is a single repo-wide file, not one per sdlc-tracked work item -- these run-budget rules govern the orchestrator's overall pacing for ANY task it works through in this repo during one run, sdlc-tracked or legacy proposal-folder alike. Say this explicitly so a future run doesn't assume budgets are sdlc-only. (Contrast with the Delegate section's task-packet/implementer mechanism, which genuinely IS sdlc-tracked-only -- don't blur that distinction, just note that budgets are a different, repo-wide axis.)

3. TASK-COUNT BUDGET (replaces 'substantial batch' as the primary stopping signal): the orchestrator tracks how many tasks it has completed THIS RUN (a plain running count kept in its own working context for the session, not a new persisted field -- `.sdlc/state.json` already tracks per-task status, this is just an in-session tally) and stops once that count reaches `max_tasks_per_run`, regardless of how much budget-headroom or momentum remains. This is the concrete, numeric replacement for 'don't grind through every remaining task unattended in one go' -- keep the spirit of that sentence but make the trigger a number read from config, not a judgment call about what counts as 'substantial.'

4. PER-TASK / PER-VERIFIER ATTEMPT ESCALATION: when a single task's attempt count (already tracked per-task in `.sdlc/state.json`'s `lease.attempt_count` for sdlc-tracked work; track it as an in-session count for legacy work, which has no such field) reaches `max_attempts_per_task`, the orchestrator stops retrying it automatically and escalates to its own judgment (treat this the same tier as 'a genuine blocker' in the existing text -- surface it to the user rather than continuing to spawn attempt after attempt). Same idea for `max_verifier_retries` specifically when the SS4.3 verifier-routing path is in play: if the verifier keeps failing a task past that retry count, stop retrying it against the verifier and escalate instead of looping indefinitely.

5. TOKEN/TIME BUDGET (soft): reference `token_or_time_budget.minutes` (and `.tokens`, if set -- it may be `null`, meaning not tracked) as something the orchestrator should keep a rough, approximate sense of over the run (e.g. noticing if a run has clearly run long relative to the configured minutes) and flag/log if it looks like the run is exceeding it -- explicitly NOT a hard stop condition, since there's no reliable primitive to enforce a hard cutoff mid-run. Don't overstate precision here; 'soft, approximate, logged' is the honest framing, not 'exactly tracked.'

6. UNCONDITIONAL STOP CONDITIONS (stop regardless of remaining budget headroom -- these are correctness/safety triggers, not pacing triggers): a phase boundary reached (already in the current text -- keep it, folded in here rather than dropped), plan divergence (a subagent's actual change doesn't match what the plan/design expected, a locally-plausible change that's globally wrong), an unexpected file touched outside every currently-open task's `write_paths` (a signal something drifted from scope even if the hook/verifier didn't already catch it), a test regression (something that passed before a task now fails), or an acceptance-criteria ambiguity that genuinely isn't this task's to resolve (needs a product/design decision only the user can make). These fully replace 'a visual change, a risky migration, anything worth eyeballing' as vague examples -- state them as the concrete list design-spec §7 gives, while still keeping the existing 'genuine blocker' and 'merging requires explicit go-ahead' bullets from the current text (those are still correct and not part of what this task is replacing).

7. OTHERWISE, CONTINUE AUTOMATICALLY: state explicitly (this is design-spec §7's actual point) that absent an exhausted budget or a fired stop condition, the orchestrator continues automatically to the next task rather than pausing to ask -- this is what makes the budgets a real replacement for 'substantial batch' rather than just an additional check alongside still-vague judgment calls.

8. WHAT TO KEEP AS-IS: the two bullets about 'the work is fully done and the only remaining step is merging' and the 'End every stopping point with: a short summary + a ready-to-use /continue-development prompt' closing structure are correct today and should survive essentially unchanged (light rewording only if needed for flow with the new budget-based bullets above them) -- this task is about the STOPPING TRIGGERS, not the reporting format at the end.

Write the actual prose into the existing 'Continue or stop' subsection, matching the file's existing voice/formatting conventions (bullet lists, bold lead-ins -- look at the surrounding Delegate/Verify/Update-tracking sections, especially SS4.3's just-added routing-decision prose in 'Verify', for the house style this file now uses). Do not renumber or restructure sections outside 'Continue or stop'.
non_goals: Do not modify `.sdlc/project.yaml`'s `budgets` values themselves -- read them, don't edit them; changing the actual numbers is a separate decision, not part of this rewrite.
Do not modify `.claude/agents/implementer.md`, `.claude/agents/verifier.md`, `.claude/hooks/sdlc-path-check.mjs`, or any schema file -- out of scope.

Do not modify the 'Orient', 'Resume in-progress work', 'Pick new work', 'Scaffold new work', 'Delegate', 'Verify', or 'Update tracking' sections of `continue-development.md` -- those are separate, already-done tasks (SS4.1/SS4.2/SS4.3) or out of this task's scope entirely.

Do not build any actual persisted budget-tracking mechanism (a new field in `.sdlc/state.json`, a counter file, etc.) -- the task-count/attempt-count tracking described here is meant as in-session orchestrator bookkeeping (prose instructions for how a future orchestrator run should behave), not a new piece of machinery to implement in code.

Do not actually run a live multi-task orchestrator loop to test that `max_tasks_per_run` really stops it after N tasks -- that live behavioral test is the orchestrator's own follow-up verification after accepting this task (same pattern as SS4.1/SS4.2/SS4.3's self-referential edits), not something for you to execute as part of this packet's own verification.

No section of `continue-development.md` other than 'Continue or stop' is modified (Orient, Resume in-progress work, Pick new work, Scaffold new work, Delegate, Verify, and Update tracking all remain byte-for-byte unchanged).
No file other than `.claude/commands/continue-development.md` is modified.
